title: scigrid-de: Monte Carlo storm-stress EENS (modelled outage probabilities, reduced 6 h horizon, 350 samples)

base_scenario.name: scigrid-de Monte Carlo storm-stress base (snapshots 0-5)
base_scenario.description: Base scenario for a StormRisk Monte Carlo study on the PyPSA SciGRID-DE example (reduced 6-snapshot horizon). Load shedding at VOLL. Outages are sampled by StormRisk from the modelled distributions in 'sampling' (same RTS-96-derived classes as studies/scigrid-de-storm-stress.json). n_samples=350 was sized from a measured pilot: 8 single-threaded solves of this 6-snapshot horizon took 3.56-3.81 s each after a 7.13 s first solve, so 350 solves (all sampled states are distinct) fit a ~25 min single-threaded budget.
assumptions: SciGRID-DE (PyPSA example, 2011 data) is a research model of the German transmission grid; results are not statements about the real German system.

outage_classes.name: lines-storm
outage_classes.source: MODELLED author-selected whole-horizon stress probability, not observed or calibrated. Context only: IEEE RTS-96 Table 12 (Grigg et al., The IEEE Reliability Test System-1996, IEEE Trans. Power Syst. 14(3):1010-1020, 1999; https://labs.ece.uw.edu/pstca/rts/rts96/Table-12.txt) lists branch outage rates 0.24-0.54 /yr and typical durations 10-16 h (some 35 h), giving stationary unavailability of order 1e-4 to 1e-3 via lambda*r/8760. q=0.01 is deliberately larger, an illustrative assumption, not a weather multiplier inferred from RTS-96.

outage_classes.name: transformers
outage_classes.source: MODELLED assumption, not observed data: IEEE RTS-96 transformer branches (Grigg et al. 1999, Table 12: 0.02 outages/yr x 768 h) give q ~ 1.75e-3; rounded to 0.002 and not storm-scaled (substation equipment assumed less weather-exposed than overhead lines).

outage_classes.name: nuclear
outage_classes.source: MODELLED assumption: IEEE RTS-96 generator reliability data (Grigg et al. 1999, Table 6), 400 MW nuclear unit forced outage rate 0.12. Not German fleet statistics.

outage_classes.name: coal
outage_classes.source: MODELLED assumption: IEEE RTS-96 (Grigg et al. 1999, Table 6), 350 MW coal/steam unit forced outage rate 0.08. Not German fleet statistics.

outage_classes.name: gas
outage_classes.source: MODELLED assumption: IEEE RTS-96 has no gas units; the 197 MW oil/steam forced outage rate 0.05 (Grigg et al. 1999, Table 6) is used as a proxy for mid-size thermal plant.

outage_classes.name: oil
outage_classes.source: MODELLED assumption: IEEE RTS-96 (Grigg et al. 1999, Table 6), 20 MW oil combustion turbine forced outage rate 0.10.
